question: Why does increasing connectedness show no joins
expected: Automatic inter-letter joins remain suppressed below JOIN_PRINT_CONN_FLOOR. Changing 0.1 to 0.3 may therefore show no joining difference.

question: When does joining begin
expected: Eligible pairs become candidates for joining. Distance, source compatibility, letter type and attachment geometry must still pass.

question: Why did the letter shapes change too
expected: Generic fallback selection can switch towards cursive forms. This changes more than the number of connectors.

question: Can you make this hand more connected
expected: More eligible joins are likely. Even connectedness of 1 does not force every adjacent character to connect.

question: Show only the contribution of added joins
expected: Zero suppresses probabilistic synthesis joins while retaining the profile's print or cursive classification. This is a cleaner isolation than crossing the profile thresholds.

question: Stop long unnatural connections
expected: Reducing it rejects longer horizontal reaches between letters. Increasing it permits more distant eligible attachments. Other gates still apply.

question: Make the writer upright and then more slanted
expected: Increasing magnitude increases horizontal shear with height, moving tall strokes more than baseline points. Slant caps and style calibration can limit or modify the result.

question: Write the same text at two sizes
expected: Larger physical x-height enlarges glyphs and advances, generally increases path length and causes earlier wrapping. Ruling and bounds fitting can override the apparent requested size.

question: Fit the paragraph into a narrower area
expected: Narrower width causes more line breaks. It does not simply squeeze every glyph horizontally.

question: Separate the words more clearly
expected: Larger values increase word gaps and can cause additional wrapping. They change layout rather than the captured character shapes.

question: Make the writing tighter or looser
expected: These constrain the gap used in advancing between stored glyphs. Tightening can increase collisions; loosening can fragment the appearance of words and increase width.

question: What prevents overlapping letters
expected: Increasing it pushes overlapping glyph extents farther apart. Reducing it permits closer placement. The guard uses geometric extents rather than semantic understanding of letters.

question: Make the writing mechanical or variable
expected: Increasing it increases positional, angular and scale perturbations and baseline drift. It does not control only one kind of variation.

question: Change position variation alone
expected: Increasing it increases glyph displacement without directly changing the rotation and scale multipliers.

question: Vary individual letter angles
expected: Increasing it increases local angular variation, distinct from the writer's overall slant.

question: Vary individual character sizes
expected: Increasing it increases local size variation, potentially changing clearance and appearance.

question: Make the baseline wander gradually
expected: Higher persistence retains drift velocity longer and produces more correlated movement. It acts on velocity, not simply on baseline position.

control: Drift bound plus or minus 0.25 x-heights
question: Keep the writing near its baseline
expected: Smaller bounds restrict wander. Larger bounds permit greater vertical displacement and can reduce clearance between lines.

question: Increase separation between lines
expected: Increasing the addition in (ascender - descender + clearance) times x-height increases synthesis pitch. Later ruling placement can alter final spacing.

question: Repeat exactly the same generation
expected: Fixes pseudorandom choices for the same inputs and execution path. Changing it changes variants and perturbations. Branch changes can still alter random-number consumption.

question: Show the uncorrected extracted style
expected: Disabling it removes the automatic shear and extent correction. The visible effect depends on the writer's stored reference measurements and cache state.

question: Prefer personal variants and then readable fallbacks
expected: Higher anchoring strength generally favours cleaner representative or fallback forms. It can reduce personal variation and changes the permitted slant. It is not a universal vertex interpolation.

question: Why does this profile use many anchors
expected: Moving the thresholds changes how median prior distance maps to automatic anchoring. An explicit stored legibilityLambda can bypass the automatic calculation.

question: Use a real representative instead of a prototype
expected: Selects the preferred stored representative, medoid or prototype, where available. Missing or rejected representatives still trigger fallback.

question: Accept more of the writer's own shapes
expected: Increasing the limit permits less typical representatives. Decreasing it can cause more generic fallback use.

question: Use only one version of the letter a
expected: Reducing the pool makes the character more repetitive. The retained glyph's quality matters more than the count alone.

control: Remove one character from a temporary profile
question: What happens when this letter was never captured
expected: Exercises missing-character fallback. The output may remain readable while becoming less specific to that writer.

question: Repair one ambiguous letter
expected: Applies stronger anchoring at selected text positions. Neighbouring joins and spacing can change too.

question: Generate quickly and then search more
expected: More trials provide more candidate opportunities and cost more inference time. The internal best score cannot worsen if the original candidate set is retained, but physical quality need not improve.

question: What does automatic repair contribute
expected: Disabling it reveals the best initial candidate. Enabling it permits targeted regeneration accepted by the full joint score.

question: Allow more correction attempts
expected: Increases the repair budget without guaranteeing improvement or a global optimum.

question: Repair one weak position or several
expected: Larger values modify more positions per trial, potentially improving readability while changing more personal geometry.

question: Prioritise text over writer identity
expected: Requires a small scoring-logic edit. A weighted or alternative combination can select different candidates from the same pool without changing trained weights.

question: Compare the ink and shape classifiers
expected: Changes which saved checkpoint judges photographed lines. Labels and confidence can change without retraining. Use that model's corresponding class mapping.

question: Does identity depend on pen thickness
expected: Enabling normalisation removes much of the original stroke-width information. It can improve robustness or discard useful cues, depending on the checkpoint and image.

question: Classify the same skeleton at different widths
expected: Larger widths thicken the reconstructed image and can close gaps. Smaller widths can lose small details after resizing. Changes occur in discrete kernel-size steps.

question: Compare saved text recognition models
expected: Changes the existing reader and potentially its transcript and confidence. The model object must actually be reloaded; a filename edit alone is insufficient.

control: Ink weighted versus equal line pooling
question: Why should a long line count more
expected: Equal weighting increases short lines' influence. Ink weighting increases dense or long lines' influence. The page result can change while every line prediction stays unchanged.

control: Lines included in the page vote
question: What if a crop is poor
expected: Excluding a crop changes the evidence and pooled probabilities. Keep the excluded crop visible rather than presenting removal as an unexplained accuracy gain.

question: What counts as evidence for weighting
expected: Raising the threshold counts more grey pixels as ink and can change relative line weights. It does not itself alter the classifier input pixels.

control: Whole line versus a shorter crop
question: How much handwriting is needed
expected: Less content generally supplies less evidence, but confidence is not guaranteed to fall smoothly. Keep crop preparation consistent.

control: Explicit blur contrast or brightness transformation
question: What happens with a poor photograph
expected: Can reveal recognition sensitivity without retraining. Stronger transformations may erase strokes, close gaps or change background estimates. These are explicit input edits rather than existing universal request sliders.

question: Can the system say it does not know
expected: Requires decision-logic addition. Reject below a threshold instead of always naming the maximum-softmax class. Raising the threshold increases abstention without improving the probabilities themselves.

question: Handle a stronger local shadow
expected: Smaller windows follow local illumination more closely but can follow ink itself. Larger windows preserve broader structures but miss rapid lighting changes.

question: Retain faint handwriting
expected: A higher ratio threshold generally retains more foreground, including noise. A lower threshold can erase faint strokes. Requires a local decision edit rather than a currently exposed request field.

question: Make the crop darker or lighter
expected: For darkness between zero and one, reducing the exponent strengthens intermediate darkness. Increasing it weakens darkness. The exponent acts on darkness, not directly on brightness.

question: Why did the page rotate by ninety degrees
expected: Lowering the margin accepts weaker quarter-turn evidence. Raising it makes turning more conservative.

control: Deskew range minus four to plus four degrees
question: Read a more tilted page
expected: A wider search handles greater global tilt at extra work, but may admit other objective maxima. It does not fix perspective or curved baselines.

question: Straighten the page more precisely
expected: Smaller increments provide finer angular search and more computation. They do not guarantee a better estimate on an ambiguous page.

question: Recover a faint line
expected: Lowering it admits weaker peaks and possible false lines. Raising it can drop faint genuine lines.

question: Separate two close lines
expected: Lowering it allows closer centres but can split one line's ascender, body and descender bands. Raising it can merge nearby true lines. P is estimated line pitch.

question: Stop splitting one line into several
expected: Lowering the threshold makes shallow-valley merging more aggressive. At 1.0, this merging loop is effectively disabled.

question: Avoid mistaking letter height for line spacing
expected: Raising the pitch floor rejects more letter-sized peak gaps, but can reject genuinely tight line spacing.

question: Remove ruling while keeping handwriting
expected: Smaller limits remove shorter straight structures and may remove genuine underlines or strokes. Larger limits retain more printed marks.

question: Make the cut avoid ink more strongly
expected: Increasing it gives closed-mask ink a stronger penalty relative to other costs. The path may make longer detours.

question: Keep boundaries near the middle
expected: Increasing it resists detours. Reducing it allows low-ink routes farther from the midpoint.

question: Make the boundary smoother
expected: Increasing it penalises vertical movement more. Reducing it permits locally jagged routes.

question: Bend around a narrow tall stroke
expected: Increasing it permits steeper row changes between columns. Reducing it limits how quickly the seam can react. The called function's default is not necessarily the active caller value.

question: Stop cuts threading through tiny stroke gaps
expected: Larger closing seals more gaps but can join neighbouring structures. Smaller closing preserves narrow passages.

question: Why was a fragment assigned to this line
expected: Raising it recognises fewer overlaps as substantial. Lowering it lets smaller overlaps affect reference ownership. This is not simply a more-correction slider.

question: Keep short lines or punctuation
expected: Lowering it retains smaller candidates and more artefacts. Raising it can discard genuine short lines.

control: Solid crop limits 15 percent and three times median
question: Why was a dark block rejected
expected: Lowering limits makes rejection more aggressive. Raising them retains denser crops. Both conditions must pass; an all-rejected fallback returns the original candidates.

question: Draw the same path more slowly
expected: Changes pen-down command feed. Digital geometry should remain the same; physical time, ink deposition and tracking can change.

question: Spend less time between strokes
expected: Changes pen-up feed. It should preserve intended drawn geometry, but carriage dynamics still matter.

question: Start before the pen settles
expected: Shorter dwell reduces waiting and can produce weak or missing stroke starts. It does not directly command contact pressure.

question: Travel sooner after lifting
expected: Shorter dwell reduces waiting but can produce travel marks if clearance has not been achieved.

question: Avoid unnecessary pen lifts
expected: Increasing it keeps the pen down over more short endpoint gaps, reducing toggles and adding connectors. This is separate from synthesis connectedness.

question: Close an almost complete loop
expected: Increasing it closes more near-loops. Excessive values can add unwanted closing strokes.

question: Reduce tiny movement commands
expected: Increasing it removes more short moves through decimation and can lose detail. It is not the extraction-stage Douglas Peucker tolerance.

question: Reduce pen-up travel
expected: Can reorder or reverse strokes while retaining much of the visible geometry. It changes execution order and potentially joins and physical ink effects.

question: Move writing away from an edge
expected: Changes placement and usable space. A narrower usable width can also change wrapping.

question: Put the next result below the previous one
expected: Moves the job vertically. It is a placement change rather than a writer-style change.

question: Fit a different paper ruling
expected: Changes ruling-based sizing. Line height can affect both letter size and placement.

question: Compare natural clearance with ruled spacing
expected: Changes line placement. Tighter ruling can bring adjacent ascenders and descenders together.

question: What happens when text does not fit
expected: Automatic fitting can shrink the output and mask an earlier size increase. Inspect the reported placement and scale.

question: Why run the cam after the switch changes
expected: Alters extra motor run after confirmed pen-up. It is distinct from the generated G-code settling dwell.
Larger tolerance retains fewer vertices and can remove fine curvature. Smaller tolerance retains more raster detail and noise.
Larger angles permit sharper chain reconnections. Smaller angles leave more separate strokes.
Changes estimated baseline and x-height, affecting many downstream normalised measurements.
Increasing it favours cuts through lower connectors more strongly.
Increasing it prevents narrow cells but can force boundaries away from the best local gap.
Larger limits admit broad valid forms and more multi-letter bad cuts. Smaller limits can reject genuine wide glyphs. Both numbers are width limits.
Larger pools preserve more variety and potentially poor variants. Smaller pools increase repetition.
Stricter filtering can improve consistency while discarding valid personal variation.
More smoothing can remove jitter and flatten distinctive corners or small features.

question: A JSON edit has no immediate effect
expected: The active in-memory profile is the intended temporary version.

question: A checkpoint filename changes while the old weights remain loaded
expected: The actual model object and its class mapping have been replaced consistently.

question: An edited profile reuses an older correction
expected: The cache key uses author and rendering scale, not every profile value. Recompute the affected correction where required.

question: New spacing limits or glyph metadata appear ineffective
expected: The cached gap range has been recalculated for the comparison.

question: Changing a module variable does not change a bound default
expected: The active call passes the intended value, or the function has been redefined through an appropriate reload.

question: New settings do not affect a saved job
expected: A new job was generated with the changed settings.

question: Automatic selection compensates for a deliberate change
expected: The direct comparison uses one candidate and repair disabled before full-system search is restored.

question: A branch change alters subsequent random choices
expected: The seed is fixed, while recognising that this does not guarantee every later glyph choice remains identical.

question: An explicit size or pitch change is rescaled later
expected: Final machine placement and scale are inspected as well as synthesis output.
